## Source access limitation

I retrieved and read the complete dataset row for **`public_swe_96`**, including its problem statement, reference patch, evaluation tests, and clarification policies. **I could not retrieve the specified agent trace**, so I cannot responsibly give a chronological account of Claude’s actions or its final outcome.

The supplied S3 location returns **HTTP 404 `NoSuchBucket`** through both standard S3 URL formats. I also checked the publisher’s Hugging Face files and the current and older HiL-Bench repositories; I found no downloadable copy of this run. The repository documents where trajectories are written during evaluation, but does not link to the requested precomputed trace.

## What the accessible source establishes

### The task

The task concerns **`protonmail/webclients`** and is titled **“Implement proper Punycode encoding for URLs to prevent IDN phishing attacks.”**

The problem statement describes inconsistent handling of internationalized domain names in external-link confirmation. In particular, a clicked element may expose both a browser-normalized URL and its original authored `href`. It also identifies inconsistent hostname matching for nested subdomains and possible failures on malformed URL strings.

The requested changes were:

- Implement `punycodeUrl` in `packages/components/helpers/url.ts` to produce an ASCII-safe hostname while preserving the relevant URL components.
- Implement `getHostnameWithRegex` in the same file to produce the matching key used by domain checks.
- Update `useLinkHandler` to apply punycode conversion to external links using the canonical link source.
- Preserve authored deep-link navigation behavior.
- Emit an error notification and stop processing when no URL can be extracted from the target. [1]

### The reference behavior and evaluation checks

The dataset specifies the following expected outputs:

| Case | Expected behavior |
|---|---|
| `https://www.mail.proton.me` | Hostname matching key: `proton` |
| `https://calendar.proton.me` | Hostname matching key: `proton` |
| `https://secure.login.example.co.uk` | Hostname matching key: `example` |
| `not-a-valid-url` | `data:,not-a-valid-url` |
| `:::invalid` | `data:,:::invalid` |
| `https://www.äöü.com/` | `https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com` |
| `https://www.äöü.com/path/` | `https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com/path/` |
| `https://www.äöü.com/a/b/?k=v#end` | `https://www.xn--4ca0bs.com/a/b/?k=v#end` |

Thus, the reference policy removes the separator only when the parsed path is exactly `/`; it preserves trailing separators on deeper paths. The reference patch selects the canonical link source with `encoded || raw`. [1]

**These are benchmark expectations—not observations of the agent’s implementation, questions, or received feedback.** In particular, the dataset’s clarification policies do not establish that the agent asked about them or was given them during this attempt.

## What cannot be established without the trace

The accessible material does not show:

- Which files the agent inspected or which tools it called.
- Whether it invoked `ask_human`, what it asked, or what replies it received.
- What code it changed.
- Which tests it ran or their results.
- Where its implementation diverged from the expected behavior.
- Its final submission or the evaluator’s outcome for `pass_3`.

A **reachable trajectory URL or an upload of the `ask_human/pass_3` artifacts**, ideally including the evaluation result, is needed to produce the requested factual chronology. Substituting the reference patch for the agent’s actual work would misrepresent the source.

# HiL-Bench: Usage Guide

HiL-Bench tests whether coding agents recognize when human clarification is necessary. It covers SQL and software-engineering tasks, each containing an ambiguity or obstacle that requires clarification.

Resources:
- [Research paper](https://static.scale.com/uploads/67a153343e046988406ef320/HiL_Bench.pdf)
- [Public task collection](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ScaleAI/hil-bench)

## Evaluation modes

| Mode | Information available to the agent |
|---|---|
| `baseline` | The original task, with unresolved blockers |
| `full_info` | The task plus explanations resolving its blockers |
| `ask_human` | The original task and a clarification tool |

## Installation and configuration

1. Initialize a virtual environment using `uv`.
2. Duplicate `.env_template` as `.env`, then add credentials for your providers.
3. Obtain the dataset from Hugging Face and save the task inputs locally. The repository does not bundle that dataset.
4. Set `hosting.type` explicitly in every agent YAML:

   | Hosting selection | Required configuration |
   |---|---|
   | `litellm_proxy` | Define `LITELLM_BASE_URL`. |
   | `provider_direct` | Leave `LITELLM_BASE_URL` unset. |
   | `self_hosted` | Supply `agent.model.api_base` or `hosting.api_base_env`. |

5. Prepare agent configurations and `config_mappings.yaml`, using `config_mappings.example.yaml` as a reference. Configurations may distinguish task categories, evaluation modes, models, and prompts.

   Restrict changes to prompts and LLM settings in the supplied example YAMLs; preserve every other field. Edited prompts must retain their original placeholder variables.

6. Prepare `judge_config.yaml` from its example. This configures the model behind the clarification tool and also requires an explicit hosting selection.

   For self-hosting, agent endpoints may use `agent.model.api_base` or an environment variable named through `hosting.api_base_env`. The clarification service instead uses `hosting.self_hosted_base_

The task concerns **`protonmail/webclients`** and is titled **“Implement proper Punycode encoding for URLs to prevent IDN phishing attacks.”**

The problem statement describes inconsistent handling of internationalized domain names in external-link confirmation. In particular, a clicked element may expose both a browser-normalized URL and its original authored `href`. It also identifies inconsistent hostname matching for nested subdomains and possible failures on malformed URL strings.

The requested changes were:

- Implement `punycodeUrl` in `packages/components/helpers/url.ts` to produce an ASCII-safe hostname while preserving the relevant URL components.
- Implement `getHostnameWithRegex` in the same file to produce the matching key used by domain checks.
- Update `useLinkHandler` to apply punycode conversion to external links using the canonical link source.
- Preserve authored deep-link navigation behavior.
- Emit an error notification and stop processing when no URL can be extracted from the target. [1]
